title: Free cotangent model and derived scalar cancellation along a ring retraction
statement: Let $A\to B$ and $j:B\to D$, $r:D\to B$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings with $rj=\mathrm{id}_B$. Let $P_\bullet=P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(B/A)$ and $K=s(\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B)$ be the standard cotangent representative of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], with Kähler differentials as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. In the derived categories of ordinary modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], use derived scalar extension as the universal total left derived functor of termwise extension [def-weil-module-base-change]. The complex $K$ has free $B$-module terms, is zero in positive degrees, and is K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Its termwise scalar extension $K\otimes_{B,j}D$ likewise has free $D$-module terms and is K-flat. The derived-to-ordinary comparison maps identify the iterated derived scalar extension $(L_{B/A}\otimes_{B,j}^{\mathbf L}D)\otimes_{D,r}^{\mathbf L}B$ with the localization of $(K\otimes_{B,j}D)\otimes_{D,r}B$. The degreewise formulas $(k\otimes d)\otimes b\mapsto r(d)b\,k$ and $k\mapsto(k\otimes1)\otimes1$ define inverse $B$-linear chain isomorphisms between that complex and $K$. They induce a canonical isomorphism $(L_{B/A}\otimes_{B,j}^{\mathbf L}D)\otimes_{D,r}^{\mathbf L}B\cong L_{B/A}$ in $D(B)$. No flatness of either ring map and no Tor-vanishing hypothesis are required.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], write $P_n=A[E_n]$ and $K^{-n}=\Omega^1_{P_n/A}\otimes_{P_n}B$, with zero positive terms; its localization is $L_{B/A}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] with $R=A$, $T=E_n$, $S=B$. After exchanging the two tensor factors, it gives the basis $e_x=\mathrm dx\otimes1$ of $K^{-n}$ for $x\in E_n$. Thus each term is free, with no finiteness restriction on $E_n$.

source.place: Tags 08PM (definition-standard-resolution), 08PN (definition-cotangent-complex-ring-map); algebra.tex Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), arbitrary-variable form as in the cited node.

proof.text: Put $E=K\otimes_{B,j}D$, termwise as in [def-weil-module-base-change]. In each degree its basis consists of $e_x\otimes1$. Explicitly, if $k=\sum_x a_xe_x$ has finite support, send $k\otimes d$ to the finite family $(j(a_x)d)_x$; its inverse sends $(d_x)_x$ to $\sum_x e_x\otimes d_x$. Bilinearity and the balancing relation make these inverse maps. The differential is $d_E(k\otimes d)=d_K(k)\otimes d$, so $E$ is also zero in positive degrees.

source.place: Tag 08PN (definition-cotangent-complex-ring-map), term description; more-algebra.tex Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change), termwise extension of a K-flat model.

proof.text: Every free module is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. Apply [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] first over $B$ to $K$, then over $D$ to $E$. Both complexes are bounded above by degree $0$, so both are K-flat in the ordinary-module sense [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. This uses flatness of the individual free terms, not flatness of $j$ or $r$.

source.place: Tag 064K (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism); free modules are flat as in algebra.tex Tag 051G (lemma-local-artinian-characterize-flat).

proof.text: Write $F_j$ and $F_r$ for the chosen universal derived scalar extensions and $Q_B,Q_D$ for localization. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-scalar-extension-counit] to $j$ and $K$, obtaining $c_j:F_j(Q_BK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_DE$. Apply it again to $r$ and $E$, obtaining $c_r:F_r(Q_DE)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_B(E\otimes_{D,r}B)$. Hence $c_r\circ F_r(c_j)$ identifies the iterated derived scalar extension with $Q_B(E\otimes_{D,r}B)$. These are precisely the derived-to-ordinary counits; the second application is justified by K-flatness over $D$, proved in Step 3.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change), proof computing LF on K-flat complexes; derived.tex Tag 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes).

proof.text: In each degree define $u((k\otimes d)\otimes b)=r(d)b\,k$ and $v(k)=(k\otimes1)\otimes1$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] applies: inner balancing follows from $r(j(a)d)b\,k=r(d)b\,(ak)$, using $rj=1$, and outer balancing follows from $r(dt)b=r(d)r(t)b$. Additivity and $B$-linearity of $u$ follow from the formula. For $v$, $(ak\otimes1)\otimes1=(k\otimes j(a))\otimes1=(k\otimes1)\otimes a$, proving $B$-linearity. Now $uv(k)=k$, while $vu((k\otimes d)\otimes b)=(r(d)b\,k\otimes1)\otimes1=(k\otimes1)\otimes r(d)b=(k\otimes d)\otimes b$. Pure tensors generate, so both composites are identities. Finally $d_K(r(d)b\,k)=r(d)b\,d_K(k)$, and $d(v(k))=v(d_Kk)$. Thus $u,v$ are inverse chain maps.

source.place: Tag 08R1 (lemma-bootstrap), last displayed cancellation; elementary tensor-balancing verification of that cancellation.

proof.text: Apply the localization functor of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to the inverse chain maps of Step 5. Composing $Q_B(u)$ with the comparison $c_r\circ F_r(c_j)$ of Step 4 gives the asserted isomorphism to $Q_BK=L_{B/A}$. The maps are specified by their formulas and the comparisons by the derived counits, so this is the canonical isomorphism for the specified derived scalar extensions. The proof has imposed neither a flatness condition on the ring maps nor a Tor-vanishing condition.

The only citer, cotangent-bootstrap, uses (ι_1, μ) and needs exactly α: F(L⊗^L D) ≅ L_{B/A} in D(B). Step 1: coherence gives P_n = A[U P_{n-1}], and the basis leaf (any variable set, any P-algebra) gives free terms. Step 2: basis of K⊗_{B,j}D via (j(a_x)d)_x; I checked balancing and the inverse. Step 3: free ⇒ flat, and bounded-flat-kflat (= Stacks 064K) over B and over D, both complexes bounded above by 0. Step 4: kflat-scalar-extension-counit applied to (B,D,j,K) and (D,B,r,E), with no flatness of the ring maps; c_r∘F_r(c_j) is well typed. Step 5: I re-derived inner and outer balancing, B-linearity of v, vu = uv = id and the chain-map property. Step 6: Q_B is a functor, so the composite is the stated isomorphism. Edge cases: non-flat j (Z → Z×Z/2), non-flat r (k[ε] → k), zero rings, infinite bases. No duplicate in the DAG, including the sibling transitivity-vanishing node and lem-sfb-scalar-extension-kflat.
